description: NEPTUNI is a science and technology team focused on building, competing, and innovating through space science, engineering, and technology. We bring together young people with diverse skills to develop creative, practical solutions to real world challenges using NASA’s open data and resources.
summary:
NEPTUNI is an interactive educational experience that aims to bring 11- to 14-year-old schoolchildren closer to space exploration by telling the story of the equipment NASA left on the Moon and Mars and the scientific discoveries it made possible.

The project develops a catalog of 15 space missions: six lunar and nine Martian. Through interactive 3D reconstructions, visitors can explore each piece of equipment, rotate the models, identify their components, and learn about their objectives, functions, and discoveries. In addition, the character Neptunito guides the experience through simple explanations, archival photographs, and information sources.

We tackle the challenge of transforming scientific and technological information into an accessible, visual, and entertaining experience that sparks students' curiosity. It includes an interactive demonstration with the Sojourner rover, which helps users understand how the APXS spectrometer works and the communication difficulties between Earth and Mars.

Its importance lies in bringing science, technology, and space exploration closer to new generations through interactive learning.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS – NEPTUNI

What it does and how it works

NEPTUNI is an interactive educational platform that brings space exploration closer to 11- to 14-year-old schoolchildren through 3D models, guided storytelling, and learning experiences based on real NASA missions.

It features a catalog of 15 missions: six related to the Moon and nine to Mars. Visitors can select a mission, explore its three-dimensional reconstructions, rotate the models, and inspect their components to discover what function they served and what scientific advances they made possible.

The experience includes a reading panel organized by topics and steps, accompanied by Neptunito, a guide character who explains the discoveries, presents historical evidence, and connects each component to its scientific purpose. It also lets users resume the tour where they left off.

Innovation and the Sojourner pilot tour

Its main innovation is linking each part of a space mission to the scientific discoveries it made possible. Rather than simply displaying 3D models, NEPTUNI invites users to investigate what function each component served and why it mattered.

One example is the Sojourner rover pilot tour, which lets users identify the APXS spectrometer, learn about the analyses performed on Martian rocks, and explore evidence from the mission. It also includes a mini-game in which the user sends commands to the rover and comes to understand the 10- to 15-minute delay in communications with Mars, as well as Pathfinder's role as a radio relay.

Educational benefits

NEPTUNI turns scientific and technological information into a visual, interactive, and accessible experience. It makes it easier to understand space engineering, robotics, astronomy, and scientific instruments, encouraging self-directed learning and curiosity about the exploration of other worlds.

Expected impact

The project seeks to inspire scientific and technological vocations in new generations, bringing the history of space exploration closer to students through digital resources that let them learn by exploring, observing, and experimenting.

Tools and technologies

It is built on a web architecture run through a local Node.js server, with components developed in JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. It integrates a 3D model viewer, interactive panels, visual reconstructions, archival photographs, and an educational mini-game. The interface is adapted for computers and mobile devices, with keyboard navigation and touch controls.

Design criteria and testing

We prioritized scientific accuracy, clarity of content, accessibility, and user experience. The information in the Sojourner tour was cross-checked against NASA, JPL, and NSSDCA sources. We also carried out functional tests in Chrome, on both desktop and mobile devices, verifying navigation, tour continuity, interaction with the models, keyboard controls, and photo generation.

NEPTUNI combines science communication, 3D technology, and interactive learning to turn the history of space exploration into an educational experience that invites users to discover how science works.

Team, roles, and contributions

Anthony Heredia · Concept, Neptunito, and script |Team leader

Defines the space-archaeology approach, creates Neptunito, and writes his messages. Prepares the video script and voice-over with Andrés.

Gianfranco Tolentino · Architecture and flows
Defines the wireframes, the navigation between the catalog and the mission cards, and the Sojourner interactions in the viewer.

Guillermo Pilares · UI and front end
Implements the home page, the catalog, the mission cards, the 3D viewer, the language selector, the user interface, and the mini-game integration.

Thays Cruzado · UX and animation
Defines where Neptunito appears, prepares his gestures and sequences, improves the video game, creates the site's flow diagrams, and tests the experience on mobile.

Mixu Alarcón · Research and content
Cross-checks the mission sources and the references for each part. Prepares the texts for the mission cards, including the explanation of the APXS.

Andrés Zelada · Visual resources, 3D, and video
Prepares the photographs and 3D models, reviews their integration into the viewer, and edits the demo video.

Artificial Intelligence Tools and Contributions

  • OpenAI · ChatGPT: Assisted with educational storytelling, scientific content simplification, UI/UX analysis, interface improvement recommendations, project documentation, and presentation scripting.
  • Anthropic · Claude: Supported frontend development, code debugging, UI/UX improvements, interactive functionality, and the creation and integration of Neptunito's 2D animation into the demonstration video.
  • Google · Gemini: Assisted with scientific research, information organization, project planning, task distribution, and technical documentation.
  • ElevenLabs: Used for AI-generated English voice-over narration for Neptunito in the 30-second project demonstration video.

AI Usage Statement

Artificial intelligence tools were used to assist our team throughout the research, design, development, and audiovisual production processes. The six team members directed the project, made the final creative and technical decisions, and reviewed the scientific information using NASA, JPL, NSSDCA, and other documented sources.

AI served as a supporting tool to improve productivity, accessibility, and educational communication, while the project's concept, objectives, and final implementation remained under the team's responsibility.
